A ballot argument will not be accepted unless accompanied by this completed typed form, which shall contain the
printed name(s) and signature(s) of the person(s) submitting it or, if submitted on behalf of a bona fide association of
citizens, the name of the association and the printed name and signature of at least one of its principal officers.
Please make sure you are using proper format before submitting to the City Clerk's Office.

This measure is a reasonable update to Brisbane's Business License Tax to ensure that
businesses contribute their fair share toward City Services. It raises fees that haven't been
adjusted since 1983 and simplifies the rate structure.
Careful consideration was given to supporting smaller businesses, those that generate sales tax,
and the current and future industries within our City limits.
Importantly, the tax measure introduces a new "cost of operations" methodology to include
businesses that don't report sales, such as laboratories, start-ups, and research and
The City's Business License Tax is a general tax, meaning all revenues are deposited into the
City's General Fund and used for general purposes. Accordingly, a general tax must be approved
by a majority of voters casting ballots on the measure.
Updating the Business License Tax is a response to the growth we've seen and anticipate in our
commercial sector. These updates are aligned with rates charged by nearby cities, and
consistent with Council goals for the sound fiscal health of our City.
